sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Deepak Chemtex is a real specialty-colourant manufacturer with a strong low-debt balance sheet, but FY2026 is a contraction, not an uninterrupted growth story. Group revenue fell 14.9% to Rs 67.64 crore and owner profit fell 33.3% to Rs 8.25 crore. CFO improved, yet finished goods nearly tripled and free cash flow remained negative during expansion. Watch for utilization and cash returns from new facilities; no purchase recommendation follows from a low headline P/E. [S1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Deepak Chemtex Limited, incorporated 1997, ISIN INE0RDM01013, BSE SME 544036, listed 6 December 2023. It is not Deepak Nitrite’s similarly named Deepak Chem Tech subsidiary. Group Indian GAAP includes 90%-held DCPL Speciality Chemicals and two overseas subsidiaries. Parent and group series are separated. Cutoff 20 October 2026; five-year horizon,15% nominal pre-tax hurdle and Rs 5 lakh position assumed. Official lot 800 shares. Rs 93.80 on 19 October is a dated secondary observation, not verified official BSE close. [S1][S2][S5][S6][S7] Secondary dated history now covers 54 observed dates in the 60-session comparison. Missing rows are not zero-filled; the observed-only 5% exit estimate exceeds 20 sessions. G4 remains Conditional and L is 2, not NS merely because official turnover is absent. [S6][S9]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.46 and GQS 5.55 use the preferred five-year revenue window and verified organic subsidiary origins. L is conditionally 2 from secondary observed-only capacity; IAS remains NS because current commissioning cost/funding, deposit restrictions and minority value allocation are materially uncertain. Canonical weighting, coverage and bounds are retained; no missing factor is reweighted.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The business manufactures colorants for food, drug, cosmetics, cleaning, agriculture and other applications, with customer-specific purification and chemistry. Household/industrial cleaning represented 48.53% of FY2023 sales, so this is not predominantly a pharmaceutical growth exposure. Domestic manufacturing,90%-held DCPL and overseas distribution create intercompany flows: parent FY2026 revenue is Rs 53.50 crore versus group Rs 67.64 crore. Eliminate internal sales when estimating accessible external demand. [S1][S3]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Customized formulations, customer audits and qualification can make switching inconvenient. Historical product breadth expanded and export customers provide distribution access. Counterevidence is substantial: FY2023 top customer 25.59%, top ten 76.41%, and no long-term contracts; product quality does not prove pricing power. Current concentration is not disclosed in the reviewed report, which repeats older product/segment statistics. MOAT5 reflects useful process/customer capabilities without a demonstrated dominant franchise. [S1][S3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Business revenue was Rs 29.56 crore in FY2021, Rs 54.11 in FY2022, Rs 46.70 in FY2023, Rs 49.35 in FY2024, Rs 79.45 in FY2025 and Rs 67.64 in FY2026. The preferred five-year CAGR is 18.01%, mapping to REV7. DCPL and South West were newly incorporated and Atlas newly established, so the group expansion is not identified as purchased revenue; intercompany trading eliminates on consolidation. Parent-only growth is not the full economic business. Growth remains volatile: FY2026 revenue fell 14.9%, core EBIT fell 38.9% and owner PAT fell 33.3%. No upward trajectory adjustment is applied. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: FY2024 management proposed another 1500 MT facility and large solar savings. FY2026 says solar is operating, but Unit 3 commercial production still depends on regulatory/environmental approvals; five products are planned. Atlas Tints USA is an additional customer-access investment. CWIP Rs 5.62 crore and annual fixed-asset/CWIP additions Rs 12.02 crore are real funding commitments, not evidence of successful utilization. Demand, yields, saleable output and return on this capital must be demonstrated before extrapolating capacity into revenue. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: March promoters hold 73.05% and declare no pledge or convertibles. This is a dated disclosure, not October clearance. Secretarial audit specifically identifies missing overseas annual performance reports for two subsidiaries. Parent subsidiary loans are Rs 22.50 crore without stipulated repayment/interest schedules; consolidation removes the receivable but not minority-allocation risk in 90%-held DCPL. Actual family pay Rs 1.0175 crore is 12.3% of owner PAT; proposed combined ceiling Rs 2.4 crore is not actual pay. Rs 50 crore related-trade authorization is a ceiling, not an order book. Independent-director changes and the August company-secretary resignation merit continuity monitoring, not presumed wrongdoing. [S1][S5] RHP identifies DCPL’s outside 10% as held by promoter Trishla Baid, not an unrelated minority investor. [S3] September 22 voting confirms all five AGM resolutions passed, including the MD/WTD reappointments and material DCPL related-party authorization. Approval is not evidence of actual transaction value or fair pricing. [S12][S13]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Reported FY2026 CFO Rs 6.257 crore versus group PAT Rs 8.469 crore gives 0.739 x; two-year conversion is 0.439 x. Inventory absorbed Rs 9.327 crore despite falling sales; finished goods rose Rs 4.036 to 10.798 crore. Receivables released Rs 3.776 crore, but over-six-month balances increased Rs 0.783 to 2.834 crore; over-one-year balances are only Rs 0.1217 crore. Other current assets contain capital advances falling Rs 2.13 crore; removing this from operating cash gives an analyst sensitivity of Rs 4.127 crore, without changing total cash. Fixed-asset cash spend is Rs 12.023 crore, so reported FCF is negative Rs 5.766 crore. Cash-flow closing balance agrees with the balance sheet. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At secondary Rs 93.80 and 10,864,000 ordinary shares, equity value is Rs 101.90 crore and owner P/E about 12.36 x. Reported EPS7.80 uses profit before minority; owner EPS is about 7.59. This 2.7% difference matters for a clean denominator but is not a critical misstatement. Core operating EBITDA is Rs 11.316 crore excluding all other income, conservative because export incentives may recur. Cash/debt bridge ranges from net cash Rs 0.455 crore excluding deposits to Rs 8.585 crore including all disclosed deposits, whose availability is not verified. Annual scenario models include working capital, capex, tax, interest and net debt but remain sensitivities using a secondary price, not entry targets or an IAS score. [S1][S6][S7] The revised full annual model starts actual ₹29.6511 crore operating WC and separately models gross debt and available-deposit cases. Future project-completion cash is explicitly varied beyond revenue-linked capex; existing capital advances/CWIP are not spent twice. Half-year draws/repayments enter simultaneous interest and tax. Bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹36.68/₹164.10/₹359.91 imply five-year IRRs -17.12%/11.84%/30.86%. The 2% economic minority proxy is stressed at 10%; it is not a claim that DCPL is 98%-owned. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Finished-goods buildup may signal slower sell-through before new capacity adds more supply. A20% inventory markdown is Rs 4.11 crore pre-tax, abouthalf owner PAT, and new plants could absorb capital before approvals or customer qualification. Currency gains and deposit interest cushion reported profit but cannot replace manufacturing earnings. Low debt and cash deposits are meaningful counterweights: this is not currently a high-leverage distress case. A severe loss of major customers or prolonged approvals would invalidate recovery assumptions. [S1][S3]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: No 5 x or 10 x probability is assigned. Those outcomes require five-year per-share growth of 38.0% or 58.5%, respectively. Latest sales and core earnings are falling, while new capital has not yet generated a proven return. A plausible upside path needs commissioned capacity, durable customer wins, inventory normalization and limited dilution. A favourable industry forecast alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Next reporting cycle: group and parent sales, core margins excluding FX/interest, inventory ageing and NRV, overdue customers, and CFO after excluding capital advances. Require Unit 3 consent/commissioning notices, saleable capacity and yields, customer qualification, project cost and utilization. Verify foreign-reporting remediation, actual remuneration, minority-party pricing, current pledges and subsidiary loan terms. Obtain official BSE60-session turnover, traded lots, circuit frequency and spreads before sizing. [S1][S5]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Quality watchlist with balance-sheet strength but unproven expansion returns. BQS5.46 and Growth Quality 5.55 are supported with medium confidence; IAS remains NS. All applicable research stages were substantively reviewed, including historical restatements, subsidiary origins, governance, cash classification, ownership, annual valuation scenarios and tradability gaps. Deep status is not a purchase recommendation. Current remaining-cost, deposit and minority-economics gaps are retained after complete linked operating/funding/terminal models; thin trading independently constrains implementation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Live issuer reports were recovered after the website migrated and legacy PDF links returned 404. Historical financial statements were OCR-checked; prospectus tables were read through the web cache. Annual narrative contains stale dates, optimistic growth language despite contraction and a dental-material R&D paragraph inconsistent with the colourants business. These indicate disclosure-control weakness but do not alone invalidate reconciled statements. Current commissioning, primary September ownership, BSE liquidity and deposit restrictions remain unverified. No input CSV or secondary financial ratio is labelled verified. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S8] Post-annual refresh recovered primary September 21 proceedings, September 22 voting, September 28 trading-window notice and October 6 depository certificate via a legitimate mirror. None provides a current funded commissioning or deposit-restriction bridge. The insider trading-window closure is not a suspension of public trading. [S10][S11][S12][S13]

GOV.reason: Disclosed family ownership, no March pledges and explicit RPT approvals are positives. Missing overseas reports, unscheduled subsidiary loans and minority allocation require caution. No severe abuse demonstrated. RHP identifies the outside 10% of DCPL as held by promoter Trishla Baid; this sharpens pricing/capital-allocation scrutiny without establishing abuse.

MOAT.reason: Customer qualification and customized chemistry create friction; no long-term contracts, historical concentration and absence of verified pricing power limit moat strength.

REV.reason: Preferred five-year business revenue CAGR FY2021 Rs 29.5566 crore to FY2026 Rs 67.6387 crore is 18.01%, mapping to 7. Subsequent subsidiaries were established organically; internal sales eliminate on consolidation, so new subsidiaries alone do not invalidate the series. FY2026 contraction and volatile intervening years preclude an upward trajectory adjustment. No acquired revenue identified.

DUR.reason: Specialized product expansion and USA customer access are tangible avenues. Unit 3 approvals and customer adoption remain conditional; no quantified contracted backlog supports a stronger score.

CAP.reason: New capital is rising as operating earnings fall; one-year incremental NOPAT proxy is negative and commissioning is not complete. Net cash allows investment, but returns on the new cohort are unproven. Not a persistent CAP<=3 override.

CASH.reason: CFO is positive and FY2026 collections improved, but two-year conversion is only 0.439 x and historical conversion is weak. Finished-goods inventory nearly triples and capital-advance release helps reported CFO. No persistent<=3 flag.

BAL.reason: Debt is only 0.71 crore versus reported cash 4.02 crore and additional deposits 5.27 crore; even cash excluding deposits exceeds debt. Expansion and unclear deposit restrictions prevent a higher score.

EXEC.reason: Solar and overseas presence progressed, but current sales/profit contracted and Unit 3 commercial delivery remains conditional. Promotional growth language is not evidence that milestones were delivered.

EARN.reason: Owner PAT declined 33.3% and core EBIT about 38.9%; FX gains cushion results. Long-run profits remain positive, but latest operating growth quality is weak.

R.reason: Remaining commissioning costs and approvals, current availability of financial deposits, and allocation of future DCPL value to the promoter-held minority are not sufficiently bounded. The completed annual scenarios and minority/cost sensitivities expose these uncertainties rather than establish a point return, recovery floor or reverse-valuation score. Secondary price provenance alone is not the reason for NS.

valuation.opening_WC_formula: Inventory 20.5358 + receivables 16.3884 + supplier/employee advances 1.0821 + GST refund 0.8988 + prepaid 0.0209 + operating security deposits 0.5373 - payables 7.9045 - operating current liabilities 1.6659 - current gratuity/expense provisions 0.1197 - noncurrent gratuity 0.1221. Excludes tax, accrued FD interest, capital advances, financial deposits and the ambiguous government-authority balance 0.9619; the latter exclusion is conservative for future cash requirements, not a finding of impairment.
notes: Opening actual balances are reconciled to the annual notes, not forecast WC ratios applied backward. No IPO proceeds added again.

The ₹0.7201 crore capital advance and ₹5.6172 crore CWIP are already paid or booked; neither is deducted again. Future capex at 8/8/10% revenue is an analyst maintenance/growth assumption; the separate ₹3/5/8 crore completion reserve is unverified remaining-cost sensitivity, not a disclosed project commitment. Severe and two-way sensitivities extend this to ₹10 crore.

Available-cash cases include only cash/current banks, then current deposits, then all deposits. Current restrictions are unverified; no separate terminal deposit salvage is added to cash already used in a scenario. No FD interest income is assumed.
11% interest uses opening gross debt plus half of draws less half of repayments, solved with 25% positive cash tax. Cash floor ₹0.3 crore; new borrowing is conditional, not committed.
Impairment is a noncash reduction of opening usable WC, charged to earnings and added back in CFO; replacement funding appears once through delta WC. No impairment tax shield.

Terminal group equity equals EBITDA times multiple plus modeled cash less debt. A 2% group minority-value haircut is an explicit economic proxy, not the actual 10% ownership of DCPL; sensitivity at 10% bounds more value accruing in that subsidiary. No dividends.
limitations: Remaining commissioning costs, regulatory approvals, plant returns and current deposit restrictions remain unverified. These gaps, not secondary quote provenance alone, prevent point investment factors.
Future margin, capex and working-capital ratios are analyst sensitivities; no independent peer-supported terminal value or asset recovery floor is asserted.
